To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the PageRank computation can be significantly simplified by exploiting the fact that most of the links point to pages on the same host; (2) the topic of a text can be identified by utilizing multiple PageRank vectors; (3) the text structure of Web pages is governed by a law that can be used to separate short from long text, which in turn can be applied for accurate main content identification.

the PageRank vector of the Web graph can be approximated by a single vector that is derived from the PageRank vector at the host level, that the topic of a Web page can be determined by the PageRank vector corresponding to the topic, and that the text structure of a Web page is a combination of short text and long text, with the long text containing the main content.

the link structure of the Web is governed by two principal motivations: “link to own page” and “link to relevant page” and that the text structure of the Web can be described by the following three classes: “short text”, “long text” and “boilerplate”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality of search engines by utilizing the structure of the Web and its text.
the question how to exploit Web structure to improve search quality in an efficient way.
quantitative strategies to improve search quality, based on the fundamental observation that the creation process and usage patterns of Web pages are governed by statistical laws.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

I show that Web search can be improved by utilizing some fundamental properties of human behavior, which are theoretically justified and relatively easy to apply, and that the processes of creating and browsing HTML text can be described as a combination of browsing for information and browsing for links, which is reflected in a corresponding combination of two different text types.
this thesis is about the quantitative exploitation of human behavior on the Web.
the Web is a very complex system that is still not well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed methods for improving search quality that are both theoretically and empirically justified, and are easy to apply in practice.
we have shown that the Web can be exploited in a quantitative manner to improve search quality.
we have developed a new approach for improving search quality, which is based on the observation that the Web is a human artifact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human Web is much more structured than it appears at first glance.
the Web, despite its complexity, has a lot to tell us about human behavior.
the Web can be seen as an information source that is governed by statistical regularities.
